data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English clif, meaning 'cliff' or 'near to the river'. This name was common among the ancient Celts and was borne by several saints. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. data.cultural_impact: The name Clyde has a strong association with the ancient Celtic people due to its Old English roots. It has a sense of strength and solidity, suggesting a connection to the land and the natural world. In pop culture, the name is most famously associated with Clyde Dolan, an American inventor, who was a central figure in the 1972 film "The Poseidon Adventure". This film highlighted the name's connection to the water, adding to its cultural significance.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Clyde carries a spiritual significance due to its association with several early Christian saints. Saint Clyde of Iona, for example, was an Irish pilgrim monk who founded the monastery on Iona in the 6th century. Clyde's name embodies the early Christian ideal of living near the water - in this case, the Irish Sea - and remaining spiritually grounded. Additionally, the name's association with cliffs speaks to the idea of rising above life's challenges and keeping a firm foundation in faith.
